questions.question: Is Robot Framework a Turing-complete language?

options.text: Yes, it supports all common control structures
No, it only supports basic sequential execution
options.explanation: Robot Framework is Turing-complete and supports IF, FOR, WHILE, and other control structures

options.text: Only when using Python libraries
options.explanation: Robot Framework itself is Turing-complete with native control structures

options.text: Yes, but only in user keywords, not in test cases
options.explanation: Control structures can be used in both test cases and keywords

questions.question: What is the purpose of IF statements in Robot Framework?

options.text: To control flow by allowing certain keywords to run only when specific conditions are met
To define variables conditionally
options.explanation: While variables can be set in IF blocks, the primary purpose is controlling execution flow

options.text: To handle errors and exceptions
options.explanation: Error handling uses different mechanisms; IF is for conditional execution

options.text: To iterate over lists of values
options.explanation: Iteration is done with FOR loops, not IF statements

questions.question: How are conditions in IF statements evaluated in Robot Framework?

options.text: As Python expressions
As Robot Framework keyword calls that return boolean
options.explanation: Conditions are Python expressions, not keyword calls

options.text: As JavaScript expressions
options.explanation: Conditions are evaluated as Python expressions

options.text: As string pattern matches
options.explanation: Conditions are Python expressions that evaluate to boolean

questions.question: What optional clauses can be used with an IF statement?

options.text: ELSE (for alternative actions when condition is false)
ELSE IF (for checking additional conditions)
THEN (to mark the start of the true block)
options.explanation: Robot Framework doesn't use THEN; the block starts after the condition

options.text: ELIF (shorthand for else if)
options.explanation: Robot Framework uses 'ELSE IF', not 'ELIF'

questions.question:
```robot
IF ${score} >= 90
    Log    Grade A
ELSE IF ${score} >= 80
    Log    Grade B
ELSE
    Log    Grade C or below
END
```

What is logged if ${score} is 85?

options.text: Grade B
Grade A
options.explanation: 85 is not >= 90, so the first condition is false

options.text: Grade C or below
options.explanation: 85 >= 80, so the ELSE IF condition is true

options.text: Both Grade A and Grade B
options.explanation: Only the first matching condition executes

questions.question: What is an inline IF statement?

options.text: A simplified IF statement for single conditional keywords that doesn't require END
An IF statement that can be written in a single line with END
options.explanation: Inline IF doesn't use END at all

options.text: An IF statement inside a keyword argument
options.explanation: Inline IF is a simplified syntax for conditional execution

options.text: An IF statement that executes faster than regular IF
options.explanation: Inline IF is syntactic sugar; performance is the same

questions.question:

It's a syntax error; IF must span multiple lines

options.text: It requires ENDIF instead of END
options.explanation: Inline IF doesn't require any closing token

options.text: It can only be used in test cases, not keywords

questions.question: What is the purpose of FOR loops in Robot Framework?

options.text: To repeat a set of keywords multiple times, iterating over a sequence of values
To execute keywords in parallel
options.explanation: FOR loops execute sequentially, not in parallel

options.text: To define multiple test cases at once
options.explanation: FOR loops are for repeating keywords within execution, not defining tests

options.text: To handle errors in a loop until success
options.explanation: FOR loops iterate over values; error handling uses different mechanisms

questions.question: How many types of FOR loops does Robot Framework have?

options.text: Four: FOR-IN, FOR-IN-RANGE, FOR-IN-ENUMERATE, FOR-IN-ZIP
Two: FOR and FOREACH
options.explanation: Robot Framework has four FOR loop variants

options.text: One: FOR-IN with different options
options.explanation: There are four distinct FOR loop types

options.text: Three: FOR-IN, FOR-EACH, FOR-WHILE
options.explanation: The four types are FOR-IN, FOR-IN-RANGE, FOR-IN-ENUMERATE, and FOR-IN-ZIP

questions.question: What is the purpose of FOR-IN loop?

options.text: To iterate over a list of values
To iterate over a range of numbers
options.explanation: FOR-IN-RANGE iterates over number ranges; FOR-IN iterates over lists

options.text: To iterate over list values and their indexes
options.explanation: FOR-IN-ENUMERATE provides indexes; FOR-IN only provides values

options.text: To iterate over multiple lists simultaneously
options.explanation: FOR-IN-ZIP handles multiple lists; FOR-IN handles single lists

questions.question: What is the purpose of FOR-IN-RANGE loop?

options.text: To iterate over a range of numbers
To iterate over a list of values
options.explanation: FOR-IN iterates over lists; FOR-IN-RANGE iterates over number ranges

options.text: To iterate over a range of dates
options.explanation: FOR-IN-RANGE specifically handles numeric ranges

options.text: To iterate over dictionary keys in a range
options.explanation: FOR-IN-RANGE creates numeric sequences

questions.question: What is the purpose of FOR-IN-ENUMERATE loop?

options.text: To iterate over a list of values and their indexes
To count how many items are in a list
options.explanation: FOR-IN-ENUMERATE iterates with both index and value, not just counting

options.text: To iterate over enum types
options.explanation: It provides list indexes and values, not enum type handling

options.text: To iterate over a range of numbers
options.explanation: FOR-IN-RANGE iterates over numbers; FOR-IN-ENUMERATE provides list indexes

questions.question: What is the purpose of FOR-IN-ZIP loop?

options.text: To iterate over multiple lists simultaneously
To iterate over compressed files
options.explanation: ZIP refers to zipping lists together, not file compression

options.text: To iterate over lists in reverse order
options.explanation: ZIP combines multiple lists; it doesn't reverse them

options.text: To iterate over a list faster than FOR-IN
options.explanation: ZIP is for handling multiple lists together, not performance

The index of the current item

With individual values listed directly

questions.question: What is the purpose of WHILE loops in Robot Framework?

options.text: To repeat keywords as long as a condition is met, when the number of iterations is not known in advance
To iterate over a known list of values
options.explanation: FOR loops iterate over known values; WHILE loops repeat while a condition is true

options.text: To pause execution for a specified time
options.explanation: WHILE loops are for conditional iteration, not delays

options.text: To execute keywords in the background while other keywords run
options.explanation: WHILE loops run sequentially, not in parallel

questions.question: What is a typical use case for WHILE loops?

options.text: Scrolling down a page until a certain element is visible
Processing each item in a known list
options.explanation: Known lists are better handled with FOR loops

options.text: Executing setup actions before a test
options.explanation: Setup actions use Test Setup, not WHILE loops

options.text: Defining multiple similar test cases
options.explanation: WHILE loops are for conditional iteration during execution

questions.question:
```robot
${element_visible}    Get Element Visibility    <locator>
WHILE    not ${element_visible}
    Scroll Down
    ${element_visible}    Get Element Visibility    <locator>
END
```

When does this WHILE loop exit?

options.text: When ${element_visible} becomes true or the iteration limit is reached
After exactly one scroll
options.explanation: The loop continues while the element is not visible

options.text: Never; it's an infinite loop
options.explanation: WHILE loops have a configurable iteration limit to prevent infinite loops

options.text: After scrolling to the bottom of the page
options.explanation: The loop exits when the condition becomes false or limit is reached

questions.question: What happens when a WHILE loop reaches its maximum iteration limit?

options.text: The loop exits with a failure, causing the test|task or keyword to fail
The loop continues indefinitely
options.explanation: The iteration limit prevents infinite loops by failing

options.text: The loop exits successfully and execution continues
options.explanation: Reaching the limit causes a failure, not a success

options.text: The loop waits for user input to continue
options.explanation: The loop fails automatically when the limit is reached

questions.question: Why does Robot Framework have an iteration limit for WHILE loops?

options.text: To prevent infinite loops and ensure tests|tasks do not hang indefinitely
To improve performance by limiting loop execution time
options.explanation: The limit is for safety, not performance optimization

options.text: To enforce best practices in test design
options.explanation: While it encourages good design, the primary purpose is preventing hangs

options.text: To save memory by limiting loop iterations
options.explanation: The limit is primarily to prevent infinite loops

questions.question: What does the BREAK statement do?

options.text: Stops the current loop and exits it immediately
Skips the remaining part of the current iteration and continues with the next
options.explanation: CONTINUE skips to next iteration; BREAK exits the loop entirely

options.text: Pauses the loop for debugging
options.explanation: BREAK exits the loop; it doesn't pause

options.text: Marks the test as failed and stops execution
options.explanation: BREAK only exits the loop; it doesn't fail the test

questions.question: What does the CONTINUE statement do?

options.text: Skips the remaining part of the current iteration and continues with the next iteration
Stops the loop and exits it immediately
options.explanation: BREAK exits the loop; CONTINUE moves to the next iteration

options.text: Continues execution after an error
options.explanation: CONTINUE is for loop control, not error handling

options.text: Resumes a paused loop
options.explanation: CONTINUE skips to the next iteration within a running loop

questions.question:

What prevents this from being an infinite loop?

The WHILE True condition eventually becomes false

options.text: The Scroll Down keyword eventually fails

questions.question:

options.text: The Log and Append keywords still execute
options.explanation: CONTINUE skips all remaining keywords in the current iteration

options.text: An error is raised
options.explanation: CONTINUE is normal loop control; no error occurs

FOR loops (FOR-IN, FOR-IN-RANGE, FOR-IN-ENUMERATE, FOR-IN-ZIP)
WHILE loops
BREAK and CONTINUE statements
